# Every fixed-core sigma trade is generated by alpha triangles

Date: 2026-07-27

Method: pure integer linear algebra.  No search is used.

## 0. Outcome

Fix an \((r-2)\)-set \(R\) and a set \(Q\) of outside coordinates, of
arbitrary size \(s\ge4\).  Consider every q1 diamond whose lower set is

\[
C_i=R+i
\]

and whose upper set is

\[
U_{ijk}=R+\{i,j,k\},
\]

where \(i,j,k\in Q\) are distinct and the lower root \(i\) belongs to the
upper triple.  Write

\[
z_{i\mid jk}=z_{i\mid kj}
\]

for an integral signed change in that diamond.  Positive entries are inserted
and negative entries are deleted.

The complete lower--middle--upper marginal kernel on this fixed core is
generated over \(\mathbb Z\) by the ordinary four-coordinate alpha trades.
Consequently a putative \(K_5\)- or \(K_6\)-supported portal move is not a
new linear generator.  If it cannot be executed as a sequence of currently
available alphas, its content is necessarily **nonconformal**: unavailable
intermediate alpha edges cancel only in the total signed sum.

This is exactly the algebraic shape of the portal problem left by the
isolated alternating PBBS component.

## 1. The fixed-core kernel

The diamond \(z_{i\mid jk}\) has lower vertex \(R+i\), upper vertex
\(R+i+j+k\), and the two middle vertices \(R+i+j,R+i+k\).  Hence a signed
array \(z\) preserves all three marginals if and only if

\[
\sum_{\{j,k\}\subset Q-i}z_{i\mid jk}=0
\qquad(i\in Q),                                      \tag{1.1}
\]

\[
z_{i\mid jk}+z_{j\mid ik}+z_{k\mid ij}=0
\qquad(\{i,j,k\}\in\tbinom Q3),                     \tag{1.2}
\]

and

\[
\sum_{k\in Q\setminus\{i,j\}}z_{k\mid ij}=0
\qquad(\{i,j\}\in\tbinom Q2).                      \tag{1.3}
\]

Equation (1.1) is lower-load preservation, (1.2) is upper-load
preservation, and (1.3) is middle-degree preservation: the middle vertex
\(R+i+j\) receives one endpoint from the diamond rooted at each third
coordinate \(k\).

For four distinct coordinates \(i,j,k,\ell\), the directed alpha triangle
\(i\to j\to k\to i\), with spare \(\ell\), is the signed vector

\[
\begin{aligned}
 &+z_{i\mid k\ell}+z_{j\mid i\ell}+z_{k\mid j\ell}\\
 &-z_{j\mid k\ell}-z_{k\mid i\ell}-z_{i\mid j\ell}.
\end{aligned}                                       \tag{1.4}
\]

It visibly satisfies (1.1)--(1.3).

## 2. Alpha generation theorem

### Theorem 2.1

Every integral array satisfying (1.1)--(1.3) is an integral sum of vectors
of the form (1.4).

### Proof

Choose one base coordinate \(\ell\in Q\).

First take a triple \(\{i,j,k\}\subset Q-\ell\).  By (1.2), its three
entries

\[
z_{i\mid jk},\quad z_{j\mid ik},\quad z_{k\mid ij}
\]

sum to zero.  An alpha on \(\{i,j,k,\ell\}\) whose directed triangle uses
\(\ell\) transfers one integral unit between any prescribed two of these
three entries, while all its other affected variables have upper triples
containing \(\ell\).  Explicitly, the triangle
\(i\to j\to\ell\to i\), with spare \(k\), changes the triple
\(\{i,j,k\}\) only by

\[
z_{j\mid ik}-z_{i\mid jk}.
\]

Two such transfers therefore set all three entries of this non-base triple
to zero.  They do not alter any other upper triple avoiding \(\ell\).
Repeating independently for every triple in \(Q-\ell\) leaves a kernel
element supported only on upper triples containing \(\ell\).

Now fix a pair \(\{i,j\}\subset Q-\ell\).  In (1.3), every term except
\(z_{\ell\mid ij}\) belongs to an upper triple avoiding \(\ell\), and has
already been made zero.  Hence

\[
z_{\ell\mid ij}=0.                                  \tag{2.1}
\]

For distinct \(i,j\in Q-\ell\), put

\[
w_{ij}=z_{i\mid j\ell}.
\]

Equation (1.2) on \(\{i,j,\ell\}\), together with (2.1), gives

\[
w_{ij}=-w_{ji}.                                     \tag{2.2}
\]

Equation (1.1) at \(i\) gives

\[
\sum_{j\in Q\setminus\{i,\ell\}}w_{ij}=0.          \tag{2.3}
\]

Thus \(w\) is an integral circulation on the complete graph
\(K_{Q-\ell}\).  Its integral circulation lattice is generated by directed
triangles.  But the directed triangle on \(i,j,k\) is exactly the restriction
of the alpha vector (1.4), with spare \(\ell\), to the surviving variables
\(w\).  Subtract these alphas until \(w=0\).  Every entry of \(z\) is then
zero, completing the integral elimination. \(\square\)

## 3. Consequences for portal creation

1. The octahedral four-trade is already an integral sum of two alpha
   triangles, consistently with the four-coordinate circulation theorem.
2. Enlarging one fixed Boolean interval from four to five or six coordinates
   introduces new support-minimal circuits, but no new lattice directions.
3. Since the alternating PBBS component initially contains no executable
   alpha side, any executable larger circuit touching it must be a
   nonconformal alpha sum: some positive edge of one formal alpha is cancelled
   by a negative edge of another before execution.
4. Therefore sequential alpha availability is the wrong gate.  The correct
   finite object is a signed alpha **commutator** whose total negative side is
   present even though its individual alpha summands are not.

The theorem does not prove that such a commutator exists in the PBBS factor,
nor does it classify support-minimal nonconformal sums.  It reduces that
problem to a finite Markov-circuit question with no further marginal
invariants hidden inside a fixed core.

## 4. The first explicit nonconformal circuit: a pentagon

There is a canonical \(5\leftrightarrow5\) circuit on five cyclically ordered
coordinates \(q_0,\ldots,q_4\).  With indices modulo five, take

\[
P=\{z_{q_i\mid q_{i+1}q_{i+2}}:i\in\mathbb Z_5\}
\tag{4.1}
\]

and

\[
N=\{z_{q_{i+2}\mid q_iq_{i+1}}:i\in\mathbb Z_5\}.
\tag{4.2}
\]

This is a valid simple trade.  Indeed:

- both sides use every lower root \(q_i\) once;
- on each side the actual middle endpoints consist of every cyclic pair
  \(\{q_i,q_{i+1}\}\) once and every distance-two pair
  \(\{q_i,q_{i+2}\}\) once; and
- for each \(i\), the positive variable rooted at \(q_i\) and the negative
  variable rooted at \(q_{i+2}\) have the same upper triple
  \(\{q_i,q_{i+1},q_{i+2}\}\).

Thus every lower, middle, and upper marginal agrees.  By Theorem 2.1 this
pentagon is an integral alpha sum, but not a conformal union of executable
alpha sides in general.  It is therefore the first natural candidate for a
PBBS portal after the four-coordinate transport has been exhausted.
